ADJ.title: pinyin (dictionary tones)
ADJ.why: The reading cannot be seen in the characters and the tones are part of the word. Dictionary (citation) tones, syllables separated by spaces; toneless syllables carry no mark; the spoken tones of 一 and 不 are in toneSandhi.

ADJ.title: traditional characters
ADJ.why: Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau write traditional characters; the learner meets both. The traditional form of the main meaning; other meanings in tradPerSense.

ADJ.title: reading per meaning (多音字)
ADJ.why: 长 cháng ‘long’ / zhǎng ‘to grow’, 都 dōu ‘all’ / dū ‘capital’: the reading depends on the meaning. Every reading with the senses it serves; none when all senses are read alike.

ADJ.title: traditional characters per meaning
ADJ.why: One simplified character can stand for several traditional ones: 里 is 裡 ‘inside’ but 里 ‘li (500 m)’, 周 is 週 ‘week’ but 周 ‘circuit, the Zhou dynasty’. None when every sense has the same traditional form.

ADJ.title: spoken tone of 一 / 不
ADJ.why: Dictionaries write 一 yī and 不 bù; in speech 一 is yí before a 4th tone and yì before the others, 不 is bú before a 4th tone. The spoken pinyin of the word where it differs; none for words without 一 / 不 or where the tone does not change.

ADJ.title: as a predicate
ADJ.why: Chinese adjectives are predicates by themselves, without 是: 他很高, 房子很大 (*房子是大). A few words that look like adjectives (区别词 / 非谓形容词: 所有, 最后) only stand before a noun, or with 是…的.

ADJ.title: takes 很 (degree adverbs)
ADJ.why: Most adjectives take 很, 非常, 太, 有点: a bare adjective predicate sounds like a contrast (这个大，那个小), so a plain statement takes an unstressed 很. 区别词 and words of identity (一样) take none. none: a phrase that already has its degree word (很好, 还好).

ADJ.title: reduplication
ADJ.why: Adjectives double for vividness: AA(的) for one syllable (大大的, 慢慢吃), AABB for two (高高兴兴, 漂漂亮亮), ABB with a fixed tail (红彤彤, 绿油油). A doubled adjective takes no 很. none: the word is not doubled.

ADJ.title: before a noun
ADJ.why: One syllable joins the noun directly (大房子, 新书) or with 的 for emphasis; two syllables, and anything with 很, take 的 (漂亮的房间, 很好的朋友); 多 and 少 cannot stand alone before a noun (很多人, 不少人).

ADJ.title: neutral (toneless) syllables
ADJ.why: A syllable that loses its tone in the word is short and light, and its dictionary tone does not apply: suffixes (子, 们, 么), particles (了, 吗), the second half of doubled kinship words (妈妈) and many common two-syllable words (朋友, 喜欢). The pinyin shows it without a mark; here: which syllable, and its tone when it stands alone. none: every syllable keeps its tone.

ADJ.title: erhua (-儿) form
ADJ.why: Northern speech, above all Beijing, adds a rhotic 儿 to many words (玩儿, 一点儿, 这儿); the south and Taiwan mostly do not. The form, its pinyin and where it is said; none when the word has no 儿 form in common use (or when 儿 makes another word: 头儿 ‘boss’).

NOUN.title: measure word(s), most usual first

values: place or + 里 (在学校 / 在学校里)
needs 上 / 里 … (在桌子上)

None for verbs that do not split.

VERB.title: negated with 不, 没 or both
VERB.why: 不 negates habits, wishes and the present / future, 没 past events and 有; 是 takes only 不, 有 only 没.

VERB.title: aspect particles it takes

VERB.title: kind of verb
VERB.why: Action verbs take every aspect particle, 得 and doubling; state verbs (有, 在, 记得) take few; psych verbs take 很 like adjectives (很喜欢, 很想); change-of-state verbs (醒, 到, 忘) are done at once — 了 but not 在; auxiliaries stand before another verb (会, 要, 想); 是 is the copula.
